Hi Alice - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of the call:
- Use case: AcmeHealth plans to send patient-support prompts (question/answer) and generate structured outputs for triage.
- Key requirements called out: no training on customer data, strict PII controls, data residency in US, 30+ day retention limits, and PCI/HIPAA conversation for later.

Open items we promised to confirm:
1) Exactly what is stored by Redwood for prompts and model outputs (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) Retention windows for those artifacts and whether they can be shortened or disabled.
3) Logging and access controls (who can see raw prompts/outputs).
4) Data residency and encryption posture.

I've looped in Neha from Security to provide concrete answers below on items 1-4 and attach a concise summary doc (PII_data_handling_summary.pdf). Rishi will follow up on procurement and pricing implications of Dedicated capacity / Private deployment.

Next steps:
- Neha: confirm default retention and options for suppression/shorter retention (ETA: EOD today).
- Rishi: send draft mutual action plan and preliminary cost estimate for Dedicated (ETA: Tuesday).
- Alice/Procurement: any specific legal or SOC2 evidence requests to add to the doc?

Thanks - happy to hop on a short follow-up if that helps.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs - follow-up (PII handling confirmation)

Hi Alice - thanks for the questions. Below is a concise, actionable breakdown of Redwood's current behavior and options for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This is accurate as of today; I'll keep the attached PDF (redwood-pii-handling-2028-03.pdf) in sync with any minor policy updates.

1) Hosted API (default):
- What is stored: request metadata (request id, timestamps, client id), full prompt text and generated outputs are retained in encrypted logs for abuse detection, debugging, and support triage.
- Retention window: default 30 days for prompts/outputs and associated logs.
- Use for training: we do NOT use customer prompts or outputs to train or fine-tune models unless explicit opt-in is provided via a contractual data-sharing agreement.
- Controls: customers can enable a "no-retention" or "short-retention" flag on their account prior to sending production traffic; exceptions apply for abuse monitoring for a short period (configurable in enterprise plans).
- Residency: hosted logs are stored in the region tied to the customer's account; US region options are available (US-east/us-west). We can guarantee US-only storage for accounts provisioned under our enterprise contract.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- What is stored: by default, Dedicated capacity keeps logs within the customer's dedicated pool. Redwood's control plane retains minimal telemetry for billing and health (aggregated metrics and anonymized traces) unless the customer opts into additional logging.
- Retention window: configurable by the customer; default is 90 days for audit logs, but prompt/output retention can be set to 0 days (i.e., disabled) for enterprise customers with contractual agreement.
- Use for training: not used for training.
- Residency: Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in a specified region (US-only). Data residency and isolation are enforced at the infrastructure layer.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
- What is stored: data remains in the customer's VPC/on-premise environment. Redwood's managed control plane (if used) will have metadata only; full prompts/outputs stay with the customer.
- Retention & logging: fully controlled by the customer.
- Use for training: never used.
- Residency: customer-controlled.

4) Security controls across all offerings:
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 encryption at rest for logs and backups.
- Access controls: RBAC for internal staff, customer-specific access whitelists, and SSO with SCIM for enterprise accounts.
- Key management: KMS support (customer-managed keys available for Dedicated/Private).
- Redaction & masking: we offer automated PII redaction/masking pipelines (configurable) for common patterns (SSNs, credit cards, PHI identifiers).
- Auditability: audit logs available (configurable retention). We can provide exports for SOC2/HIPAA evidence requests.

5) Evidence & artifacts we can provide quickly:
- SOC2 Type II summary + point-in-time report (SOC2_report_stub.pdf).
- Short data flow diagram showing where prompts/outputs are routed (attached: PII_data_handling_summary.pdf).
- Encryption and KMS architecture note (we can provide a deeper KMS diagram on request).

6) Policy notes & timeline:
- Default hosted retention is 30 days; enterprise contracts can reduce/disable retention for hosted or migrate to Dedicated/Private for full control.
- We will not use your prompts/outputs to train models without explicit written consent.
- ETA for providing the SOC2 evidence packet and a scoped MSA/Data Addendum: 2 business days (we can push same-day for urgent procurement).

If you want, we can produce a short customer-specific summary that you can share with Legal/Procurement that states the exact commitments we will put in the contract.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
